US imposes tariff on Finnish tourism products, industry faces cancellations and uncertainty

HELSINKI, June 8—The US government has imposed a 25% tariff on tourism products from Finland, disrupting the Finnish tourism industry and leading to mounting cancellations, industry representatives said Saturday. The measure, which took effect on June 1, affects packaged tours, guided travel experiences, and cultural excursion products sold to US-based travel agencies and consumers.

The Federation of Finnish Tourism Companies said bookings from the United States have dropped sharply since the announcement. “We have seen a 40% decline in confirmed group tours from the US market for the summer season, with many operators postponing or cancelling trips due to increased costs,” said Timo Laine, spokesperson for the federation.

The tariff is expected to impact over 150 tourism firms in Finland, including major operators such as Suomi Tours and Nordic Expedition Group. Many companies have begun scaling back operations. “We are reviewing our summer staffing levels and may need to reduce seasonal hiring by up to 20% if the situation persists,” said Marja Nieminen, CEO of Suomi Tours.

Key tourist sites that rely on US visitors, such as Lapland’s Arctic heritage centers and Helsinki’s city museums, have reported lower visitation rates this month. Local tourism workers’ unions have expressed concern about job security. “Our guides, event staff, and seasonal workers are facing an uncertain summer,” said Jussi Virtanen, chair of the Tourism Workers’ Union. “We urge both governments to resolve the dispute swiftly.”

The Ministry of Economic Affairs estimates that the US accounted for around 12% of Finland’s international tourism revenue last year. Officials said talks with US counterparts are ongoing. “We are seeking a prompt resolution and support measures for affected firms and workers,” Tourism Minister Sari Koskinen told reporters.

The tariff remains in place as negotiations continue.
